description: How SAS CLASS variables are encoded for GLM-type procedures (reference-level / GLM parameterization) and how redundant dummies are handled during selection.

glm_reference_last.title: GLM-type CLASS encoding is less-than-full-rank with the LAST sorted level as the aliased reference.
rule: PROC GLM/GLMSELECT default to GLM parameterization: a 0/1 indicator is created for every level, but the design is deliberately singular and the LAST level (by the CLASS ordering) is aliased to zero, making it the reference.
Level ordering follows the CLASS variable's formatted values (typically ascending / alphabetical) unless ORDER= changes it.
For equivalent predictions in pandas, one-hot encode and drop the reference (last) level; coefficients are then interpreted relative to that reference.
PROC LOGISTIC is different: it defaults to EFFECT coding (levels contrasted against the mean, reference gets -1), so do not assume drop-last for logistic unless PARAM=GLM is set.
pitfalls: Dropping the FIRST level (pandas get_dummies(drop_first=True) default) mismatches SAS GLM, which drops the LAST.
Assuming GLM-style drop-last for PROC LOGISTIC (which uses effect coding by default).
Unstable level ordering: sort levels deterministically so the reference is reproducible.

code: {f'{s.name}_{lvl}': (s == lvl).astype(int) for lvl in levels if lvl != ref}

reference_impl.note: Builds PARAM=GLM design columns for CLASS main effects and continuous*CLASS interactions; redundant columns are aliased via sas_rank.

redundant_dummy_aliasing.title: A candidate dummy that is collinear with the current design is redundant and must be skipped/aliased.
rule: When adding CLASS dummies during selection, a new indicator can be an exact linear combination of columns already in the model (e.g. a level fully determined by other levels within a block, or a constant within the current subset).

SAS aliases such redundant columns rather than adding them. Detect this before entry using the same relative singularity check used for continuous collinearity (see sas_singularity_rank), or by checking that the augmented design does not lose rank.
Skipping redundant dummies keeps the model rank, degrees of freedom, and selection path aligned with SAS.
pitfalls: Blindly adding every level's dummy creates a singular design and diverging coefficients.
A dummy that is constant (all 0 or all 1) within the current training rows carries no information and should be treated as redundant.
